transcript.text: Every so often when I put the washing machine on the whole kitchen power goes off and I have to go to the fuse box and flick the switch back up. It doesn't happen every time. Indesit, IWE 7 something.

⚠ Stop using this appliance
Please don't keep resetting the trip. Leave the appliance unplugged and have it checked by a qualified electrician or appliance engineer before using it again. Please do not use this washing machine again until it has been checked by a qualified engineer, as an electrical fault tripping your kitchen power is a safety risk. The most common cause for an Indesit washing machine to trip the mains supply is a 'short to earth' in one of its internal components. The heater element is the usual suspect; when water reaches it, if the insulation has failed, electricity leaks to the casing and trips your fuse box. Less commonly, it could be the drain pump or the motor. To help us understand which part might be failing, does the power trip happen immediately the moment you switch it on (before any water enters), or only once the machine has started filling with water and begins to heat it up?

It doesn't trip straight away. It always happens a few minutes into a 40 or 60 degree wash, so I assume once it's filled and started heating. It has never tripped on cold, quick 30 or rinse and spin. I'll admit I've been resetting it each time so far, and it's tripped quite a few times over the last month. I haven't smelled burning or seen any sparks.

⚠ Stop using this appliance
A burning or hot-plastic smell, smoke, scorching or melting can mean an electrical fault or a fire risk. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it (or turn it off at the fuse box), and don't run it again — not even as a test — until it has been checked by a qualified engineer. Please don't keep resetting the trip. Leave the appliance unplugged and have it checked by a qualified electrician or appliance engineer before using it again. The fact that it only trips when the water is hot and never on cold cycles points to the heater element having an internal insulation failure (a 'short to earth'). When the element heats up or gets wet, electricity leaks to the metal casing of the machine, tripping your RCD/fuse box. This is a very common fault with Indesit machines. Because this involves mains voltage and water, you must not use the machine again until it is fixed. To confirm which part has failed, please unplug the machine completely. Access the rear panel to find the heater element (the metal disc at the bottom of the drum). Disconnect its wires from the terminals on the element itself. Using a multimeter set to resistance (Ohms), measure across the two metal spades on the element; it should read between 20 and 50 Ohms. Then, touch one probe to a metal spade and the other to a bare metal part of the machine casing. If you get any reading there, that suggests the element is shorting to earth and needs replacing.
